description:
## What

`src/fetcher/request_config.cr` has two `with_*` methods that build a new `RequestConfig` by manually copying ALL 16+ fields:

- `with_retry_max_retries(max_retries : Int32)` — overrides retry.max_retries, copies every other field
- `with_redirect_allowed_domains(domains : Array(String))` — overrides redirect.allowed_domains, copies every other field

## Why

Maintenance hazard: any new field added to `RequestConfig` (or its component records) must be added to BOTH copy methods or the new field will be silently lost. The `RequestConfig` class has 19 fields today. Both copy methods are 30+ lines of repetitive boilerplate.

Functional/purity angle: this is a classic sign that the class is missing a proper copy primitive. Crystal records get `.with(...)` for free; a class with this many fields should have an equivalent.

## How

Extract a private `copy_with(**overrides)` that takes a hash of overrides and produces a new RequestConfig with the overrides applied. Or refactor `RequestConfig` to be a record (immutable, automatic `.with(field: value)` method, no manual field copying).

The class-as-record refactor is the cleaner option but touches every constructor call site. The private-helper refactor is the surgical fix.

## Counter-considerations

- Refactoring to record would change `RequestConfig.new(...)` semantics (positional vs keyword, mutability). This is a public API change.
- The private-helper approach keeps the existing API but reduces the boilerplate.

## Done when

- No manual `RequestConfig.new(timeout: @timeout, retry: new_retry, ...)` boilerplate remains
- Both `with_*` methods are short (a handful of lines each)
- Full spec suite still green
- Any new field added to `RequestConfig` automatically works with `with_*` methods
title: Refactor: deduplicate RequestConfig.with_* copy methods
